List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the November 24, 2006/Agrahayana 3, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Agro and Rural Industries; Chemicals and Fertilizers;
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests;

Total number of questions — 20
Cheating consumers through
advertisements
†*41. SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the cases of cheating of consumers through
attractive but illusive advertisements;
(b) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to ban such advertisements;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
constitute a National Consumer Protection
Regulatory Authority in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, whether Government propose
to consider any such suggestion?
Agricultural products' outlets at
stations
†*42. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether agriculture products' outlets
are being set up at railway stations;
(b) if so, the details of services and
facilities that would be made available at
these outlets;
(c) whether farmers would be benefited
by these outlets; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Pollution in Delhi
†*43. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that due to
pollution at many places in Delhi, the
atmosphere has become adverse for human
life;
(b) if so, in addition to ITO and Chandni
Chowk, the names of the places where due
to pollution the atmosphere has become
adverse for human life; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

15
(c) whether Government have traced the
reasons for pollution of the atmosphere
and if so, the details thereof?
Ganga Action Plan
*44. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) what were the objectives of the
Ganga Action Plan and the schedule of its
implementation;
(b) the total amount spent over this
project and the foreign aid component
therein;
(c) whether the Plan has been able to
achieve the stated objectives; if not, the
reasons therefor;
(d) whether it is a fact that serious
questions have been raised on the efficacy
of the project; and
(e) the steps being taken to control the
pollution in the river?
Forest clearances on fast track
*45. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government have put in
place a new policy and system to "FAST-
TRACK" all the forest clearances;
(b) how many forest clearances have
been given in Southern States in the last
two years, State-wise;
(c) out of such forest clearances, how
many were cleared under the "FAST-
TRACK" forest clearance facility;
(d) whether a system of incentives has
been offered to various officials in the
Southern region to help to bring all
applications under "FAST-TRACK" ambit;
and
(e) the details of "FAST-TRACK"
forest clearances and their negative impact
on forests?
Agriculture reform scheme
†*46. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government are
considering to implement necessary
agriculture reform scheme keeping in view
the tendency of suicides by farmers in the
country; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reform programmes to be included in this
regard?
Controlling dengue and
chikungunya
*47. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH  AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
 (a) the number of dengue and
chikungunya cases reported in the Capital
during the last three months;
(b) the number of patients suffering
from these diseases and actually admitted
in Government hospitals in the Capital and
how many of them died during that period;
(c) whether Government hospitals in the
Capital were not fully equipped to handle
such cases and a large number of patients
had to rush to private hospitals and incurred
heavy expenses which were beyond the
reach of many such patients; and
(d) the remedial steps Government
propose to take to handle such a situation
in future?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

16
NCF recommendations
†*48.SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
 (a) whether all the reports of the
National Commission on Farmers have been
received by Government;
(b) if so, when;
(c) the details of the recommendations
of the Commission and by when
Government would take a decision on them;
(d) whether it is a fact that one of the
members of the Commission has given his
own suggestions due to his disagreement
on some of the recommendations of the
Commission; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the
reaction of Government thereto?
Media campaign on World Diabetes
Day
*49. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government have recently
issued a lot of newspaper advertisements
to remember and celebrate World Diabetes
Day;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the specific cost of the
advertisements given in October, 2006;
(d) the details of cost benefit yardstick
used to assess and critically judge the utility
of such advertisements; and
(e) the details of policy formulations
behind issuing advertisements on such
disease or illness-specific days?
Measures to control dengue and
chikungunya
*50. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that viral diseases
like dengue and chikungunya created a havoc
in the country and large sections of people
fell victim of these diseases and this also
took a heavy toll of human lives;
(b) if so, whether Government had
called a meeting of all the Health Ministers
of the affected States to discuss the situation
arising out of these diseases;
(c) if so, the outcome thereof; and
(d) the steps both the Central and the
State Governments have taken to meet the
situation arising out of these diseases?
Controlling suicides
*51. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
 (a) whether suicides by farmers are still
going on in various parts of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the reasons for the large scale
suicides of farmers; and
(d) the corrective measures taken by
the Central Government in this regard?
Rural indebtedness
*52. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government are aware of
rural indebtedness which is alarmingly on
the increase in the country;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

17
(b) if so, the reaction of Government on
the dimension and prevalence of rural
indebtedness; and
(c) whether Government would declare
it a national problem and work out a national
scheme to tackle this?
Rise in prices of pulses
*53. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA:
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government have taken
cognizance of rise in prices of pulses during
the recent months;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
details of movement of prices of pulses
during the current year and the comparative
prices of pulses during the last three years;
(c) the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps being taken by Government
to assuage the price-rise of pulses?
Imbalance in agricultural cost inputs
and outputs
*54. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state the concrete steps
Government propose to take in view of
crash in prices of agricultural output and
rise in cost of agricultural input which have
adversely affected the interests of all
sections among the peasantry?
Completion of AIIMS-like institutions
*55. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
 (a) the status of completion of AIIMS-
like hospitals in six States of the country;
(b) the hindrance in the completion of
project in Orissa; and
(c) the time-frame within which this
hospital would be completed and put into
operation in the State?
Illegal trade of animals and birds
*56. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that large number
of animals and birds are illegally being
transported by trains to various
destinations in the country;
(b) if so, how many such cases had been
brought to book during the last one year;
and
(c) the strict action Government had
taken or propose to take against this illegal
trade?
Dengue prevention measures in the
country
*57. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that Government
could not foresee and prevent dengue
menace in the country;
(b) the number of persons affected
positively and those died in different
States of dengue by now due to
inadequate arrangement in Government
hospitals; and
(c) the steps being taken to prevent
recurrence of dengue in the country?

18
Effect of climate change on
agriculture
†*58. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that clear
indications of change in climate are being
noticed in the country and this has begun
affecting the agriculture of the country
adversely;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(c) whether Government have
undertaken any study about the adverse
effects on the agriculture due to climatic
changes; and
(d) if so, the details of the report in this
regard?
Doubling of Ernakulam-
Kayamkulam-Kottayam rail line
*59. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
 (a) the details of the funds allocated to
the rail line doubling work in the Ernakulam-
Kayamkulam-Kottayam sector;
(b) whether the work has commenced
on this sector;
(c) if so, the details of the work
completed, so far;
(d) the reasons for the slow progress of
the work; and
(e) the time by which the work would
be completed?
MSP of bajra and other agri-products
in Rajasthan
*60. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government are
considering an increase in MSP of bajra
and other agri-products in Rajasthan; and
(b) if not, the reasons therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Agro and Rural Industries; Chemicals and Fertilizers;
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests;
Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Small Scale Industries; Steel)
Total number of questions — 155
Reducing cost  of sunflower seeds
244. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that sunflower
seeds producing companies are selling their
products at Rs. 500 to Rs. 600 per 2 kg.
packets based on their brand names;
(b) if so, the estimated cost of producing
the seeds and profit margins enjoyed by
the manufacturers;
(c) the methodology adopted for fixing
prices and the authority which is fixing
prices of all hybrid variety seeds; and
(d) whether there is any proposal by
Government to reduce the cost of sunflower
seeds and other hybrid seeds to mitigate
the problems of farmers?
Suicides vis-a-vis loans from private
money lenders
245. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the reports of continuous farmers’ suicides
from various States;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the loan with
exorbitant interest rates taken from the
private money lenders is one of the major
causes for the distress of farmers;
(d) if so, whether Government have
taken any measure to protect the farmers
who are indebted to the money lenders;
(e) whether Government would declare
the debts taken from the money lenders as
illegal; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Liberalising trade in agriculture
commodities
246. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY :
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to liberalise the trade in agricultural
commodities;
(b) the reasons which forced
Government, hitherto, not to liberalise the
said trade;
(c) the impact of this decision on the
prices of agricultural commodities;

59
(d) whether it is not a fact that the recent
price rise is the result of the above decision;
and
(e) if so, whether Government  would
review the said decision?
MSP of wheat
247. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Minimum
Support Price (MSP) of wheat has been
raised by Rs. 100/- per quintal;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that,
considering the rising cost of fertilizers,
agricultural implements and labour, the
MSP fixed is very low; and
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Subsidies to farmers for increasing
wheat production
248. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal under
Government's consideration to offer liberal
subsidies to the farmers in the country to
substantially increase production of wheat
during the ensuing rabi season; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Setting up of National Agricultural
and Technology Mission
249. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO : Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a National
Agricultural and Technology Mission is
being proposed to be set up to revive the
farm sector;
(b) if so, the details of the mandate,
power and functions of the said mission;
(c) to what extent, it would be different
from the existing National Commission on
Farmers; and
(d) the details of strategy to strengthen
farm sector and overcome farmers' suicide?
Increasing investment in agriculture
250. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether FAO of the United Nations
has called for greater investment in
agriculture and policy support for evolving
public-private partnership in agriculture as
over 854 million people, a  large number of
them in India itself, are destined to go
hungry;
(b) if so, whether according to the
report, 40 countries including India are
facing food shortage;
(c) if so, whether Government have
examined the report; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to meet the situation?
NCF recommendations
251. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Commission
on Farmers, headed by Dr. M.S.
Swaminathan had submitted its final report;
(b) if so, whether the report has
suggested for setting up a National Food
Security and Sovereignty Board under the
Chairmanship of the Prime Minister;

60
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) the other main points mentioned by
the Commission;
(d) by what time a National Policy for
Farmers is likely to be approved and
announced; and
(e) whether Government would clear
Rs. 16978.69 crores relief package for
farmers in 31 districts across four States
plagued by distress deaths?
Assistance for dairy development in
Madhya Pradesh
†252. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of amount to be spent
on dairy development out of the funds
allocated for agricultural development
during the Eleventh Five Year Plan;
(b) the amount proposed to be allocated
to Madhya Pradesh in this regard; and
(c) the amount allocated to Madhya
Pradesh for dairy development from 2004
to 2006?
Assistance to farmers hit by national
calamities
253. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there are numerous instances
of farmers committing suicide who are under
heavy debt in areas affected by natural
calamities;
(b) if so, the details thereof during the
last three years, State-wise and year-wise;
(c) whether Government have extended
any relief  to the families of the deceased
farmers;
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
during the last three years;
(e) whether there is demand for writing
off of the loans obtained by the farmers
from banks;
(f) if so, the details thereof;
(g) whether Government have expressed
its inability to accept the demand; and
(h) if so, the details in this regard?
Subsidies for wheat output
254. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether forced to import wheat for
the first time in 6 years, Government have
unveiled plan to boost wheat output by
about 7 million tonnes in the coming season
through a plan i.e. entirely subsidy-driven
costing Government Rs. 2482 crores over
three years in 138 identified districts;
(b) if so, whether this money would be
used for seed replacement, demonstration
of improved technology, micro-nutrients
and use of advanced sowing technique;
(c) if so, to what extent these methods
have been introduced; and
(d) to what extent it has been helpful in
achieving the higher production of wheat?
NCF recommendations
†255. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National
Commission on Farmers has submitted its
final report to the Government;

61
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Commission has even recommended
necessary constitutional amendments in the
interest of agriculture and the farmers;
(c) whether the Swaminathan
Commission has highlighted the
continuously declining trend of capital
investment in agricultural sector since Sixth
Five Year Plan as one of the salient reasons
for decline in agricultural production; and
(d) if so, the details thereof in the light
of above points and the effective steps
Government propose to take in this
direction?
Per-acre yield of rice
256. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India ranks
second in terms of the volume of the rice
produced but ranks sixteenth in terms of
yield of the crop per-acre;
(b) the reasons for low yield of the crop
per-acre; and
(c) the details of steps being
contemplated, if any, to improve the
scenario indicating the time-frame thereof?
Change in guidelines for assistance to
drought hit States
†257. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have brought
about changes in the existing guidelines for
one-time waiver for one year on interest
payment for kharif crops to increase the
ceiling of agriculture investment subsidy
and to provide additional assistance to
provide relief to drought hit States;
(b) if so, the complete details of
guidelines issued by the Centre; and
(c) the details of the assistance schemes
and credit schemes provided/proposed to
be provided by Central Government to the
farmers of drought hit States particularly
Rajasthan?
Relief to farmers of Uttar Pradesh
258. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
ascertained the facts on the recent media
reports on the meagre amounts being
distributed as relief to farmers in Uttar
Pradesh;
(b) whether Government have also
taken cognizance of reported corruption
by the local administrative functionary in
distributing the relief;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken to ensure
effective and efficient delivery of the relief
aid to the farmers in affected areas?
MSP of wheat and other grains
259. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have raised the

62
Minimum Support Price of wheat and other
grains, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether this MSP restores parity
between domestic and international
foodgrain prices, if not, the reasons therefor;
and
(c) whether Government would
consider to have different procurement
prices to ensure sufficient stocks of
foodgrains if intended amount of foodgrains
are not purchased on the MSP, if not the
reasons therefor?
Suicides in Vidarbha
260. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
as many as seven farmers including women
committed suicide in a single day in
Vidarbha taking the toll to 1045 since June,
2005;
(b) if so, the steps Government have
taken to provide relief to the aggrieved
families in Yavatmal region in Yavatmal
district;
(c) whether Government are also aware
that in the month of October, 2006 only,
112 suicide cases were recorded in the
Vidarbha region; and
(d) if so, whether Government would
consider complete waiver of private as well
as Government outstanding loans of
farmers, if not, the reasons therefor?
Stopping recovery of loan
†261. SHRI PYARELAL KHAN-
DELWAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that keeping in
view the case of increasing incidents of
suicides amongst farmers a National
Committee has suggested to stop the loan
recovery in the calamitous areas
immediately;
(b) if so, what are the other
recommendations of the Committee;
(c) whether it has been also stated in
the report that profit is gradually decreasing
in the agricultural sector; and
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
NCF recommendations
262. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
SHRI MOINUL HASSAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Commission
on Farmers has recommended five point
programme for rejuvenation of agriculture
sector;
(b) if so, whether Government have
prepared any plan in this direction; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Dairy development
263. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) what is the planning of Government
for dairy development in the country;
(b) the number of proposals that have
been received by Government from various
States particularly Andhra Pradesh
Government under Consolidated Dairy
Development Planning;
(c) the details of action being taken on
those proposals; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

63
(d) the effective measures being taken
by Government for achieving the objectives
and targets fixed by Government under this
scheme, State-wise?
Suicides in rural areas
264. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of causes of suicidal deaths
among the farmers in the rural areas of the
country;
(b) the details of special packages
already implemented and proposed to be
implemented for the benefit of the farmers
in the rural areas to avoid suicidal deaths;
and
(c) the details of monetary and other
relief measures already provided to the
bereaved families of farmers who died due
to suicides, State-wise and district-wise?
Crop loss in Andhra Pradesh due to
heavy rains
265. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether heavy rains have affected
crops in the country particularly in Andhra
Pradesh, this year;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the production figures of different main
varieties of paddy, fruits and vegetables
during the last three years and those
expected during 2006-07, State-wise;
(c) the details of exports of crop that
are likely to increase or decrease this year,
compared to that during the last two years;
and
(d) the assistance provided to the
affected farmers of the Andhra Pradesh?
Waiving off the farmers' loans
266. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the farmers in the country
have approached the Prime Minister to
waive off the loans given to the farmers in
view of the suicides by the farmers in the
country;
(b) if so, the amount to be waived, State-
wise and when;
(c) whether the Prime Minister has
accepted the approach and if not, the
reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps expected to be taken for
the protection of such farmers from
committing suicide and when?
Financial assistance for promotion
and development of horticulture
267. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of financial assistance
granted to the States for promotion and
development of horticulture during the last
three years;
(b) whether funds allocated to the States
have been under-utilized; and
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
and the reasons therefor?
Withdrawal of the Seeds Bill, 2004
268. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to withdraw
the Seeds Bill, 2004  as it does not allow
use of traditional seeds;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

64
Decline in purchasing power of
farmers
†269. SHRI PYARELAL KHAN-
DELWAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
the 59th report of the National Sample
Survey, the crores of farmers of the country
have to live with only Rs. 8/- a day;
(b) whether it is also a fact that a heavy
decline in the purchasing power of the
